answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake tokens that vest only after sustained useful work: like a raven returning to the same timber roost season after season, an agent builds a verifiable history of completed tasks, and each successful job adds a plume to its reputation record. New identities start with zero trust and tiny job caps, so spinning up a thousand fakes buys no influence. Influence must be earned slowly, and misbehavior burns the stake, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents keep compounding trust.
